title: Mass–energy & binding energy
examples: What is the difference between mass and energy in physics?
How do we calculate the energy released when atoms combine?
Can you explain what the binding energy curve shows?

explain.say: Today we explore the link between mass and energy. Einstein showed that these two are connected.
The equation E equals mc squared tells us the energy contained in mass. This relationship is fundamental to modern physics.
Next we look at mass defect. This is the missing mass when elements form a nucleus. It is calculated by comparing parts.
The mass defect is then converted into energy using E equals mc squared. This released energy is the binding energy. It holds the nucleus together.
The binding energy curve shows how stable different nuclei are. More binding energy means a more stable nucleus.
Think about burning fuel like wood in a campfire. The chemical energy stored in the wood is released as heat and light. This is a real-life energy release.

faq.q: What is the difference between mass and energy?
faq.a: Mass and energy are interchangeable forms of the same thing. The equation E equals mc squared shows this relationship clearly.
It means the difference between the mass of separate parts and the actual mass of the combined whole. This missing mass becomes energy.
asks: Why is the combined mass less?
What is the missing mass called?

faq.a: Yes, for a stable nucleus, the binding energy is positive. This positive value represents the energy that must be supplied to break the nucleus apart.
asks: Does a nucleus need energy to exist?
What does a positive binding energy mean?

faq.q: Does this apply to chemical reactions too?
faq.a: Yes, chemical reactions also involve mass-energy changes. However, the energy released is usually much smaller than in nuclear reactions.
asks: Are chemical bonds related to nuclear binding?

faq.q: Can you calculate the energy released from a decay?
faq.a: You need the initial and final masses to find the mass defect. Then, you use E equals mc squared to find the energy.
asks: What do I need to calculate energy release?
How do I use the mass defect formula?

facts: The relationship E equals mc squared links mass and energy.
Mass defect is the difference between predicted and actual nuclear mass.
Binding energy is the energy holding the nucleus together.
The binding energy curve peaks around iron-56 nuclei.

quiz.say: If a nucleus has a mass defect, what can be concluded about the reaction?

options.show: The energy released is proportional to the number of protons.
options.say: The energy released is proportional to the number of protons.

options.show: Energy will be released in the reaction.
options.say: Energy will be released in the reaction.

quiz.why: A positive mass defect means mass has been converted into energy, which is released.

wrong.0: This suggests the reaction is endothermic, which contradicts the concept of mass defect.
wrong.1: If the mass defect were zero, no energy would be released, which is not true for stable nuclei.
wrong.2: While protons are involved, the energy depends on the total mass defect, not just the proton count.

quiz.say: Which statement correctly describes the binding energy curve?

options.show: The curve increases linearly with atomic number.
options.say: The curve increases linearly with atomic number.

options.show: The curve shows stability only for light elements.
options.say: The curve shows stability only for light elements.

options.show: The curve shows that heavier elements are always more stable.
options.say: The curve shows that heavier elements are always more stable.

options.show: The curve shows maximum stability near iron-56.
options.say: The curve shows maximum stability near iron-56.

quiz.why: The peak of the curve indicates the most tightly bound, and thus most stable, nucleus.

wrong.0: The curve does not increase steadily; stability varies due to nuclear forces.
wrong.1: The curve covers all elements, showing stability trends across the periodic table.
wrong.2: Stability decreases for very heavy elements due to increasing repulsion.

quiz.say: If a reaction has a positive mass defect, what is the energy change?

options.show: Energy will be released in the reaction.
options.say: Energy will be released in the reaction.

options.show: The energy released depends only on the number of neutrons.
options.say: The energy released depends only on the number of neutrons.

quiz.why: A positive mass defect means the final mass is less than the initial mass, so energy must have been released.

wrong.1: This describes an endothermic process, which is opposite to energy release from mass loss.
wrong.2: If the energy released were zero, there would be no mass defect.
wrong.3: Energy depends on the total mass defect, involving protons, neutrons, and electrons.
